officialTitle: Palbociclib and Letrozole in Advanced Breast Cancer
setting: First-line advanced (no prior treatment for advanced disease)

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: In this double-blind study, we randomly assigned, in a 2:1 ratio, 666 postmenopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, who had not had prior treatment for advanced disease, to receive palbociclib plus letrozole or placebo plus letrozole.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding palbociclib to letrozole prolong PFS as initial therapy for postmenopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer?

pico.population: Postmenopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, no prior treatment for advanced disease
pico.outcomes: Primary: investigator-assessed PFS. Secondary: OS, objective response, clinical benefit, PROs, PK, safety

publications.title: Palbociclib and Letrozole in Advanced Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The median progression-free survival was 24.8 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 22.1 to not estimable) in the palbociclib-letrozole group, as compared with 14.5 months (95% CI, 12.9 to 17.1) in the placebo-letrozole group (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.46 to 0.72; P<0.001).

safety.sourceQuote: The most common grade 3 or 4 adverse events were neutropenia (occurring in 66.4% of the patients in the palbociclib-letrozole group vs. 1.4% in the placebo-letrozole group)
Febrile neutropenia was reported in 1.8% of patients in the palbociclib-letrozole group and in none of the patients in the placebo-letrozole group.

safety.description: Permanent discontinuation of any study treatment due to adverse events
safety.sourceQuote: Permanent discontinuation of any study treatment as a result of adverse events occurred in 43 patients (9.7%) in the palbociclib-letrozole group and in 13 patients (5.9%) in the placebo-letrozole group.

strengths: Double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III confirmation of phase 2 findings
limitations: OS not reported in the primary publication

clinicalImplications.text: Confirmed a substantial PFS benefit for adding palbociclib to letrozole as first-line therapy in postmenopausal ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, at the cost of more neutropenia.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Palbociclib neutropenia is frequent but febrile neutropenia is uncommon — manage with blood-count monitoring and dose adjustment rather than reflexive discontinuation.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 27959613. OS analysis not ingested.
